newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed a lacklustre session up on Thursday as limited demand drove prices higher in the absence of any real offering.

Dealers said a combination of technical factors such as month-end window-dressing, institutional short-covering and click-fund related buying had helped push up the index, which derived further support from firmer guilder bonds and gains on neighbouring exchanges.
The expected profit-taking ahead of the long weekend failed to materialise, with the index building on its opening gain of 5.79 points to 740.19 to peak at 744.08 before subsiding.
But another dealer countered that based on the U.S. inflationary outlook there was no need for a further rate hike.
An absence of major stories meant most trading interest homed in on the small caps sector, where a string of companies published 1996 results.
Delft blue pottery maker Porcelyne Fles added 0.20 to 23.20 guilders after reporting a modest 1996 profit following the previous year's loss.
Precision instruments maker Delft Instruments saw profits fall to 12.9 million guilders from a year-earlier 16.3 million and lost 0.20 to 40.00 guilders.
"We had expected some position-squaring before the long weekend in the form of profit-taking, but in the event institutions ended up short covering," one dealer said.

Another said that so-called "click funds" had triggered sustained low-level demand the entire week and this upward pressure had become more noticeable on Thursday in the absence of real selling activity.
"Another factor is the month-end effect -- players are looking to note down a high value in the books," one said.
The index would likely hover in a short-term trading range of around 742 to 748 points, he said.
Early gains were partly wiped out at midsession as players hung back ahead of U.S. weekly jobless data, but the fall had little impact as U.S. Treasuries shrugged off the news.
Petrochemicals group DSM was one of the few AEX component stocks to end the day down, but dealers said there were no special reasons behind the fall.
"It's just another indication of how volatile the market is right now," one said.
He said lingering doubts on whether the recent hike in the U.S. Federal funds rate had been enough were still unsettling the market.
Builder Heijmans dipped 0.50 to 41.0 guilders after reporting 1996 profits rose to 38.0 million guilders from a 32.7 million in 1995 and announcing a small takeover.
Among the big issues, Philips pared early gains on restructuring news and broker upgrades to end 0.50 higher at 87.50, back from the day's peak of 89.20.

Nutricia reported 1996 net profits and a five-for-one share split after close of bourse trading. The foods group said profits soared to 231.7 million guilders from a year-earlier 151.8 million, in line with forecasts.
The shares closed 10 guilders higher at 290.00.
